messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you help write a short correction for the Cedar Falls Ledger, for the local news page? our May 14 story about the Riverview Library book sale said it would open Saturday, May 18. that date is wrong: the sale opens Sunday, May 19, at 10 a.m., in the library meeting room. the story also said admission was $3, but admission is free. please make clear that these are corrections to the earlier story, not a new event announcement. keep it plain and brief, like a newspaper correction, and don't add details we haven't got. the library coordinator gave us this exact line: “The doors open at 10 a.m. on Sunday, May 19,” said coordinator Lena Ortiz. another note from the editor says: “The printed story listed a $3 admission fee; the library has confirmed there is no admission charge.” use both notes exactly as written, including the quotation marks and attribution. i don't need a headline unless one is needed to make the correction understandable. don't turn the coordinator's remark into a paraphrase or make it sound like the newspaper is quoting the editor. just make the correction clear to readers who saw the May 14 story.", "output": "Write a short, plain correction for the Cedar Falls Ledger’s local news page about its May 14 story on the Riverview Library book sale.

Correct the two errors in the earlier story: it gave the sale date as Saturday, May 18, but the sale opens Sunday, May 19, at 10 a.m. in the library meeting room; it listed a $3 admission fee, but admission is free. Make clear that this is a correction to the earlier story, not a new event announcement. Do not add details that are not provided.

Use both notes exactly as written, including quotation marks and attribution:
“The doors open at 10 a.m. on Sunday, May 19,” said coordinator Lena Ortiz.
“The printed story listed a $3 admission fee; the library has confirmed there is no admission charge.”

Keep the coordinator’s remark as a quote, and do not present the editor’s note as a quote from the newspaper. A headline is optional; include one only if needed to make the correction understandable."}]
